The proposal is to seek **robust program equilibria by having agents reason about each other’s behavior**, rather than requiring their source code to match exactly. (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11238-018-9679-3) Exact-match strategies such as CliqueBot can fail to cooperate after harmless changes such as adding comments. (https://arbital.com/p/modal_combat)

For example, **FairBot cooperates if Peano arithmetic can prove that its opponent cooperates against FairBot**. Through Löb’s theorem, this proof-based mechanism enables cooperation between different versions of FairBot, rather than only identical copies. (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11238-018-9679-3) A resource-bounded extension establishes mutual cooperation among a wide variety of unequal agents satisfying a “fairness” condition: finding a sufficiently short proof of the opponent’s cooperation must be sufficient to trigger their own cooperation, with the permitted proof length increasing with the opponent’s code complexity. (https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S0022481217000421/type/journal_article)
